compartments.title: Parser retry loop fixed
compartments.p1:
I traced the config parser's retry loop to a stale file-handle cache: reopening the same path returned the pre-edit bytes, so validation failed identically on every retry. I switched the cache key to (path, mtime) and added a regression test that edits the file mid-loop.
U: Why does it retry at all if the input never changes?
I agreed and added a terminal arm: identical input on consecutive attempts now fails fast instead of burning the retry budget.
compartments.p2:
Parser retry loop: stale file-handle cache returned pre-edit bytes. Fixed with (path, mtime) cache key + fail-fast on identical consecutive input.
U: challenged retrying unchanged input.
compartments.p3:
Fixed parser retry loop (stale handle cache); fail-fast on unchanged input.
U: why retry unchanged input

compartments.title: Queue draining benchmark
compartments.p1:
I benchmarked the work queue's drain path: 12k items drained in 840ms with the mutex held across the batch, 95ms with per-item locking and a snapshot iterator. The snapshot approach also removed the deadlock window a slow consumer could open.
U: Ship the snapshot version but keep the batch path behind a flag for the embedded target.
compartments.p2: Queue drain benchmark: batch-mutex 840ms vs snapshot 95ms at 12k items; snapshot also closes a slow-consumer deadlock window. Shipped snapshot; batch kept behind embedded-target flag.
compartments.p3:
Queue drain: snapshot iterator 9x faster, closes deadlock; shipped.
U: flag-gate the batch path

compartments.title: Log rotation ownership bug
compartments.p1:
I found rotated log files created root-owned when the service restarted under the init wrapper, breaking the reader's tail. The wrapper ran the first rotation before dropping privileges. I moved rotation after the privilege drop and asserted ownership in the health check.
U: Add the ownership assertion to the doctor command too.
compartments.p2: Log rotation created root-owned files (rotation ran before privilege drop). Moved rotation post-drop; ownership asserted in health check and doctor.
compartments.p3:
Log rotation ownership fixed (post-privilege-drop); doctor asserts.
U: extend doctor

compartments.title: Cache warmup ordering
compartments.p1:
I reordered service warmup so the token cache fills before the first request is admitted: previously the first burst raced the warmup and half the requests paid a cold lookup. Admission now gates on a warmup-complete latch with a 5s ceiling and a cold-path fallback.
U: What happens at the ceiling?
At the ceiling the latch opens regardless and the cold path serves; the ceiling exists so a broken warmup cannot hold admission closed.
compartments.p2:
Warmup ordering: token cache fills before admission (latch + 5s ceiling + cold fallback). Ceiling prevents broken warmup wedging admission.
U: probed ceiling behavior.
compartments.p3:
Warmup latch before admission; 5s ceiling, cold fallback.
U: ceiling probe
